Sara — thanks for sending these over and for the timeline. I'm available to triage and prioritize. Quick thoughts after a first pass:

Top-of-mind DPA items (we should decide "non-negotiable" vs "commercial negotiation"):
- Data residency / cross-border transfers (BannerCo: are you requiring EU-hosted endpoints?)
- Subprocessors and notification windows (we usually require 30 days notice for new subprocessors)
- Audit rights / frequency — our legal prefers annual with scoped checklists; we can be flexible on scope for production-only incidents
- Logging & retention of support traces (there's sometimes tension here; we can agree retention buckets)

For the SOW: please call out acceptance criteria for the connector, responsibilities for integration testing, and who holds the production cutover sign-off. That makes procurement and services scoping much cleaner.

Can we do a 30 min triage on Tue 2027-05-04 at 10am PT? If that doesn't work, propose two slots and we'll make it happen.

I'll loop in Ben from RevOps to ensure procurement sequencing and Laura for legal ops.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA and SOW for Redwood integration

Hi Karthik / Laura — thanks for the quick reply. We had an internal review and can offer the following movement:

- Audit scope: BannerCo can accept annual full-audit rights for security & privacy, provided that we retain the right to request a targeted, production-impact audit within a 60-day remediation window if there's a material incident.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a 30-day notice for new subprocessors, but require a 14-day objection window followed by mediation language if BannerCo objects.
- Data residency: for EU customers we require that customer data be processed and stored within EU regions unless the customer explicitly permits cross-border processing. Is Redwood able to pin EU-hosted model endpoints for BannerCo EU accounts?
- Support logs: BannerCo Legal requests a 24-month retention for support traces for compliance reasons; we understand Redwood may have cost concerns. Can we scope retention tiers in the SOW?

I've attached a slightly updated DPA with the above notes (BannerCo_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf, updated page 3/4).

> Thanks for the demo last week — the engineering team at BannerCo is excited to move forward. I'm attaching our DPA redlines...

Best,
BannerCo Legal

Subject: Re: Initial DPA and SOW for Redwood integration

Thanks — looping in Redwood legal ops detail. Quick summary of our position and suggested language to keep the deal moving:

1) Audit rights
- Our standard position: annual audit by a mutually agreed third party; targeted audits allowed for material incidents with clear scope limited to the incident areas. Suggested clause: "Targeted audits permitted upon written notice and limited to systems and timeframes reasonably necessary to investigate the incident."

2) Subprocessors
- We can accept 30-day notice. We prefer a 30-day objection window with escalation to a defined senior ops contact before formal mediation. Proposed tweak: replace "mediation" with "security-exception review" process to speed resolution.

3) Data residency
- Redwood supports pinned EU-hosted endpoints for EU customers (we have regional clusters). We'll add a SOW appendix that lists available regions and any additional costs for pinned capacity.

4) Support logs / retention
- We agree to a tiered retention table in the SOW: 6 months (default free tier), 24 months (paid retention option), and an audit-only retention export process. This preserves compliance while controlling costs.

I've redlined a SOW draft with the above (BannerCo_SOW_redline_v1.docx). Highlighted the acceptance criteria and the integration responsibilities (who owns test harness, cutover checklist, and post-cutover monitoring).

Next steps we propose:
- Karthik: run procurement timeline with BannerCo (target sign by 2027-05-27)
- Legal ops: exchange final DPA redlines by 2027-05-12 for review
- Implementation: tentatively schedule integration kickoff week of 2027-05-23 if contracts are signed

Happy to hop on the Tue slot if helpful — otherwise we can confirm the 2027-05-04 triage.

Laura Bennett
Senior Legal Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BannerCo DPA carveouts & SOW scope alignment — summary and next steps

Team — thanks for the constructive back-and-forth. Summarizing agreed points and next steps so procurement/legal teams have clear actions:

Agreed points:
- Audit: annual third-party audit standard; targeted incident audits allowed with limited scope (Laura will provide exact wording).
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice accepted; BannerCo will use a security-exception review first before mediation.
- Data residency: Redwood can pin EU-hosted endpoints for BannerCo EU customers; add appendix for region/costs in SOW.
- Retention: SOW will include a retention tier table (6 months default, 24 months paid, export for audit).

Action items & dates:
- BannerCo Legal: confirm acceptance of Laura's proposed audit wording by 2027-05-12 (Sara / Tim)
- Redwood Legal Ops (Laura): circulate final DPA redline by 2027-05-12
- Procurement (Ben): confirm ordering path and PO template; target contract signature by 2027-05-27
- Engineering (Karthik): calendar integration kickoff contingent on signature, target week of 2027-05-23

Links: HubSpot deal - https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-2147; DocuSign envelope (placeholder) - https://docusign.example/envelope/0a1b2c3d

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
